newsitem.title: KENYA: Human rights group condemns rebel abuses of Hutus.
newsitem.headline: Human rights group condemns rebel abuses of Hutus.

text.p: Amnesty International condemned on Wednesday human rights abuses by Tutsi-dominated rebels against Rwandan refugees in Zaire and called for international pressure.
The London-based human rights group said rebels had looked on while Zaireans attacked aid workers and looted aid supplies south of the northeastern Zairean capital of Kisangani earlier this week.

It said the rebel Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire (AFDL) had stopped providing security for aid workers and supplies and a lack of security inside and on the way to the camps had halted relief work in recent days.

"How many refugees have to die or suffer human rights abuses at the hands of the AFDL before world governments and intergovernmental organisations send a clear message to the AFDL that they would be held accountable for any further deaths ordered or condoned by their leaders?" it said.

"The international community should put pressure on the AFDL to recognise that refugees have a right to life and other human rights. The deliberate violation of these rights is totally unacceptable under any circumstances," it added in a statement.
"The deliberate disruption of humanitarian assistance to the refugees amounts to cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment."
Zairean villagers said on Wednesday Tutsi-dominated rebels slaughtered many Rwandan Hutu refugees at camps south of Kisangani and aid workers said they had reports up to 55,000 refugees had fled.
The villagers, travelling towards Kisangani, said a pitched battle between rebels and refugees accompanied the slaughter on Tuesday at camps near Kasese village, 25 km (15 miles) south of Kisangani.
The camps at Kasese for 55,000 Rwandan refugees have been sealed off from aid workers and journalists for three days.

But rebel leader Laurent Kabila told Reuters by telephone from Zaire's second largest city Lubumbashi that the reports were "total nonsense" and Rwandan Hutu militiamen had attacked villagers and his rebels only intervened to stop the fighting.
